title: Variable-Width Sign Extension
constraints: The low `n + 1` bits of `x` hold a signed number (width 1 to 16). Bits above them are **garbage**. Output `y` = that number sign-extended to 16 bits.
No loops or generate, and no `?:`, `if` or `case`: no mux per bit position.
hints: First clear the garbage: keep `x & mask`, where mask has n + 1 ones. `mask = (m << 1) - 1` with `m = 1 << n` (it wraps correctly for n = 15).
Then the famous trick: `(v ^ m) - m`, where m is the sign-bit position. XOR flips the sign bit, and subtracting m borrows through all the upper bits exactly when the sign was 1.
Everything is 16-bit arithmetic: one shifter, one subtractor, one XOR.
